subject: Package Development: Order of Imported Packages

messages.author: 03290ff051991093
messages.subject: Package Development: Order of Imported Packages
parts:
All,

When using devtools/roxygen2 for creating the NAMESPACE file, I've
noticed that the order of the packages specified in @import is not kept
when devtools/roxygen2 translates this to the NAMESPACE file. For example:

##' @import foo bar

Will become reverted (in NAMESPACE), since it seems to be sorted
alphabetically there:

import(bar)
import(foo)

So my question is this: Is there any way I can keep the order the same
as in the @import tag?

The reason I'm asking is that some functions are masked, e.g. `foo:f`
will mask `bar::f`, but I would like it to be the other way around.

(Of course, I could import all functions from `foo` except for `foo:f`,
but that would be a lot of typing...)

Thanks,
M

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Package Development: Order of Imported Packages
parts:
There's no way. You can use either @importFrom to pull in selected
functions, or just use foo::bar() to disambiguate in the case where
you need it - I think that's better practice anyway, since it will be
obvious which function you're using when you read the code in the
future.

Hadley

messages.subject: Reshape-reshape2 issue
parts:
Hi all,

I need to reformat some data and the notes I have show a very simple few lines of code:


Bats<-"imported file name"

Bats.melt <- melt(data = Bats)

#this fills NA with zeros - tested and works

Bats.cast <- dcast(data = Bats.melt, formula = Species ~ Location, fill =0)

dput(Bats.cast,'C:/=Bat data working/Bats_niche.robj')

write.csv(Bats.cast,'C:/=Bat data working/Bats_Niche.csv')



The DF under Variable view:
Species
Location
Date
Time


First 2 lines seem fine but the 3rd...
> Bats.cast <- dcast(data = Bats.melt, formula = Species ~ Location, fill =0)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'Species' not found

This did work some time back, but no longer sure if this was used under Reshape.
Perhaps now Reshape2 has a different syntax?  For what I coudl glean this does not seem so.

Any suggestions welcomed.

Bruce

Possibly, but you shouldn't rely on melt to pick the variables for
you. Specify one of id.vars or measure.vars.

>

>>Bats<-"Chile_AI"

Hard to see how that's useful in this context...
